userStories.title: Create model_capabilities database migration
userStories.description:
Create the PostgreSQL migration that establishes the model_capabilities table as the single source of truth for model availability. The table tracks provider identity, model metadata, probe status, and historical success/failure metrics used by computeHealth() to determine real-world availability. This is a pure database migration with no UI component.

**Convention guidance**: Follow the project's established migration pattern in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/`. Use timestamp format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` as required by CLAUDE.md. Use `TIMESTAMPTZ` (not `TIMESTAMP`) for all time columns — matches existing migrations. Use `TEXT` with CHECK constraints for enum-like columns rather than PostgreSQL ENUM types (avoids ALTER TYPE migration headaches). Column naming must use `snake_case` consistently. Default values should use `NOW()` not `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` to match existing migration conventions in 001–079.

## Context
- **Migration file naming**: Use exact timestamp format `20260425100000_create_model_capabilities.sql` in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/`. The `pg-index.ts` runner sorts numerically — timestamps (20260425100000) sort after existing sequential migrations (001–079) automatically. `checkDuplicatePrefixes()` runs at startup and will fail loudly on collisions.

- **Transaction wrapping**: Wrap the entire migration in `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` and use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` — this is the standard pattern in existing migrations. The `pg-index.ts` runner tracks applied migrations in the `schema_migrations` table (BIGINT version column), so the IF NOT EXISTS is a safety net, not the primary idempotency mechanism.

- **Column type conventions from existing migrations**: Use `TIMESTAMPTZ` (not `TIMESTAMP`) for all time columns, `TEXT` with `CHECK` constraints for enum-like values (not `CREATE TYPE` / PostgreSQL ENUMs — avoids `ALTER TYPE` migration pain), `snake_case` for all column names, and `DEFAULT NOW()` (not `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`) to match the 001–079 migration style.

- **Composite primary key note**: `PRIMARY KEY (provider, model_id)` means no separate `id` serial column is needed. Queries throughout the codebase use `$1, $2` numbered placeholders with the `pg` driver — any seed data or parameterized queries in the migration must follow this convention (never `?` placeholders).

- **CHECK constraint values must be lowercase strings**: `probe_status IN ('healthy','degraded','unavailable','unknown')` and `provider IN ('codex','claude','opencode','anthropic','openai','openrouter')` — all lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity bugs when routes or `llm-client.ts` query by status/provider.

- **NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 on counters**: `recent_success_count` and `recent_failure_count` must never be null — `computeHealth()` will do arithmetic on these columns and `GREATEST()` comparisons. Null arithmetic silently produces null results, breaking health scoring.

- **Index on probe_status**: `CREATE INDEX idx_model_capabilities_probe_status ON model_capabilities (probe_status)` — filtered queries like `WHERE probe_status = 'healthy'` are the primary read path for model selection. Consider also indexing `(provider, probe_status)` if provider-scoped health queries are anticipated, but the spec only requires the single-column index.

- **No UI, no route, no llm-client changes**: This story is a pure DDL migration. Do not touch `llm-client.ts`, `model-pricing.ts`, or any route files — those come in later stories. The migration should be self-contained SQL with no TypeScript changes.

userStories.title: Implement resolveModel function in model-registry.ts
userStories.description:
Create backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts with the resolveModel() function that looks up a requested model ID in model_capabilities and returns it if registered and not unavailable. This is the core indirection point — all downstream code paths will call resolveModel() instead of checking static arrays. The function must handle provider-prefixed IDs (e.g. 'openai/gpt-4o') by splitting on '/' to extract provider. This is a pure backend library with no UI component — API consumers receive the ResolvedModel shape which includes all DB columns plus a computed 'health' field ('healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable') for future UI status dot rendering.

**Convention guidance**: File must use named exports only (no default export) per project convention. All function parameters and return types must have explicit TypeScript annotations — no implicit `any`. Use the project's `query<T>()` and `queryOne<T>()` helpers from `../db` for database access with `$1, $2` numbered placeholders. Use `interface` for object shapes (`ResolvedModel`, `RegisteredModel`, `ModelCapabilitiesRow`) and `type` for unions (`ModelProvider`). Import from specific module paths, not barrel files.

## Context
- **File location & exports**: Create `backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts` with named exports only — no `export default`. Use `interface` for `ResolvedModel`, `RegisteredModel`, `ModelCapabilitiesRow`; use `type` for `ModelProvider` union.
- **DB access pattern**: Import `query<T>()` / `queryOne<T>()` from `../db` (see `backend/src/db/index.ts`). Use `$1, $2` numbered placeholders — never string interpolation. `queryOne` returns `T | undefined`, so map `undefined` → `null` for the public API.
- **Provider-prefix splitting**: Split on first `/` only (`requestedId.indexOf('/')`) to handle `openrouter/anthropic/claude-3` correctly (provider=`openrouter`, model_id=`anthropic/claude-3`). Query strategy: (1) try `WHERE provider=$1 AND model_id=$2`, (2) fallback to `WHERE model_id=$1` with any provider using the full original string. This handles both pre- and post-translation IDs from `pipeline.ts`.
- **Health computation**: `computeHealth()` should derive health from DB columns (e.g. `is_available`, `failure_rate`, `last_checked_at` — check the `model_capabilities` migration for exact columns). Return `'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable'`. The `allowDegraded` option defaults to `true` — only when explicitly `false` should degraded models return `null`.
- **Input validation**: Return `null` immediately for empty/whitespace-only `requestedId` (`!requestedId?.trim()`) without hitting DB. Guard against SQL injection is already handled by parameterized queries, but validate input shape defensively.
- **Snake-to-camel mapping**: DB columns are `snake_case` (`requires_subscription`, `requires_api_key`); TypeScript interfaces use camelCase with boolean `is/has/requires` prefixes. Map in the query result transformation, not via SQL aliases (keeps SQL readable).
- **Gotcha — `chatComplete` returns `ChatResult`**: This file won't call `chatComplete`, but downstream consumers of `ResolvedModel` will — ensure the `ResolvedModel` type includes enough info (provider, model_id, context_window, supports_tools, etc.) for callers to make routing decisions without re-querying.
- **Gotcha — model ID translation in pipeline.ts**: `pipeline.ts` already does Claude SDK → OpenRouter format translation (e.g. `claude-opus-4-6` → `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.6`). `resolveModel` may be called from contexts that haven't applied this translation yet, so both the bare ID and the prefixed ID must resolve to the same capability row.

userStories.title: Implement computeHealth scoring function
userStories.description:
Add computeHealth() to model-registry.ts that computes a composite health status from probe data and historical run metrics. The key invariant: a model with more than 5 successful runs in the last 7 days is never marked unavailable regardless of probe_status. This protects working models like gpt-5.4 from being hidden by stale or incorrect probe data. The returned health value ('healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable') is included in all API responses that surface models, enabling future Phase 2 UI status dot rendering (green dot for healthy, amber dot for degraded, red dot for unavailable).

**Convention guidance**: This is a pure function — takes a row object, returns a string literal union. No side effects, no DB calls. Use explicit return type annotation `'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable'`. Avoid nested ternaries — use early returns for each case. The 7-day window check should use a named constant (`const HEALTH_WINDOW_DAYS = 7` and `const MIN_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD = 5`) not magic numbers. Export as a named function.

## Context
- **Pure function pattern**: `computeHealth()` must be a synchronous, side-effect-free function with explicit return type `'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable'`. Export as named function from `model-registry.ts`. No DB calls inside — it receives a pre-fetched row object.
- **Named constants**: Extract `HEALTH_WINDOW_DAYS = 7` and `MIN_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD = 5` as module-scope `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` constants. Project convention prohibits magic numbers (see engineering standards).
- **Early return guard clauses**: Use sequential `if (...) return 'healthy'` guards, not nested ternaries or if-else chains. Each health decision is a separate block — matches the project's `clean_code` principle (functions under 40 lines, single responsibility).
- **Date arithmetic gotcha**: `last_succeeded_at` from PostgreSQL `pg` driver may arrive as a `Date` object or ISO string depending on query path. Always normalize with `new Date(lastSucceededAt)` and check for `Invalid Date` (treat as null → "older than 7 days"). Use `Date.now() - date.getTime()` for the window check — never string comparison.
- **Key invariant — success history overrides probe**: A model with `recent_success_count > 5` AND `last_succeeded_at` within 7 days must return `'healthy'` even if `probe_status === 'unavailable'`. This is the core safety net preventing stale probes from hiding working models. Place this guard **before** the probe_status checks.
- **`'unknown'` probe_status maps to `'degraded'`**: The return type union is only three values (`healthy | degraded | unavailable`). When `probe_status === 'unknown'`, map to `'degraded'` regardless of success count — allows model to appear with a warning rather than being blocked.
- **Null safety on `last_succeeded_at`**: When null, the 7-day window check must evaluate as false (model has never succeeded). This means null `last_succeeded_at` + `probe_status === 'unavailable'` → return `'unavailable'`.
- **TypeScript strict mode**: Project uses `strict: true`. Annotate the return type explicitly as the string literal union — do not let it widen to `string`. The `ModelCapabilitiesRow` type should include `probe_status`, `recent_success_count`, `last_succeeded_at` fields typed to match the DB schema.

userStories.title: Implement listAvailableModels function
userStories.description:
Add listAvailableModels() to model-registry.ts that returns filtered model rows from model_capabilities. This replaces direct reads of ALL_MODELS, SUPPORTED_MODELS, and models_cache.json for UI-facing model list endpoints. Supports filtering by provider, probe status, and an includeUnavailable flag. Each returned model includes the computed health field so API consumers (including the frontend ModelPicker dropdown) can render status indicators in Phase 2 without a second round-trip.

**Convention guidance**: Use the project's `query<T>()` helper with parameterized queries. Build the WHERE clause dynamically but safely — use an array of conditions and params, never string concatenation of user input. Return type must be explicitly `Promise<RegisteredModel[]>`. The function should accept an options object (not positional params) since it has multiple optional fields — follows the 'no more than 4 parameters' rule.

## Context
- **DB helpers**: Use `query<T>(sql, params)` from `backend/src/db/index.ts` — returns `T[]`, always `await`. Build WHERE with `conditions: string[]` + `params: any[]` pattern, push `$N` placeholders dynamically. Never interpolate user values into SQL strings.
- **`chatComplete` returns `ChatResult`**: Not relevant to this story directly, but if any downstream consumer passes model list results to LLM calls, remember `.text` accessor. More importantly here: `computeHealth()` is pure application logic — do NOT push it into SQL.
- **spec `id` is the slug**: The `model_id` column in `model_capabilities` is the canonical model identifier (e.g. `claude-opus-4-6`), analogous to spec slug convention. Use it consistently as the primary key/lookup field.
- **Options object pattern**: Accept `ListModelsOptions` interface with all-optional fields. This matches the codebase convention seen in `paginate.ts` and route query param destructuring — avoids positional param sprawl.
- **Index awareness**: The `idx_model_capabilities_probe_status` index exists. When filtering by availability (default behavior excluding `unavailable` health), consider whether the WHERE clause can leverage `probe_status` column to let Postgres use this index rather than doing a full scan + app-level filter. However, since `computeHealth()` is app-level, you'll likely fetch all/filtered rows then compute health in JS — this is acceptable for the expected table size (<200 models).
- **Empty table edge case**: A fresh install has zero rows in `model_capabilities`. Return `[]` — do NOT throw `NotFoundError` or any `AppError` subclass. This is a valid state, not an error.
- **Ordering**: `ORDER BY provider ASC, display_name ASC` in SQL for stable UI rendering. Rows with `NULL` display_name sort first in Postgres (`NULLS FIRST` is default for ASC) — this is fine per AC, but if you want deterministic order add `model_id ASC` as a tiebreaker.
- **Return type**: Explicitly type as `Promise<RegisteredModel[]>`. `RegisteredModel` must include the `health` field (computed post-query). Map DB rows to `RegisteredModel` in application code, attaching `computeHealth(row)` result to each row before returning.

userStories.title: Implement recordRunOutcome function
userStories.description:
Add recordRunOutcome() to model-registry.ts that atomically increments success or failure counters for a provider/model pair. This is called from execution-engine.ts after each story completes. If the model is not yet registered (e.g. a hidden Codex model that runs successfully), it upserts a new row — ensuring the registry learns from reality.

**Convention guidance**: Use `execute()` from `../db` for write operations that don't return rows. The upsert pattern (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE`) must use `$1, $2` numbered placeholders. The function signature follows the project convention: explicit return type `Promise<void>`, explicit parameter types. Error handling: wrap in try/catch with structured error logging — never throw from this function since it's fire-and-forget. Use `console.error` with the `[model-registry]` prefix for consistent log grep-ability.

## Context
- **Target file**: `backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts` — this is a new function added to the existing model registry module that already contains `getModelCapabilities`, `listModels`, etc.
- **DB helper convention**: Use `execute(sql, params)` from `../db` for writes (returns `{ rowCount }`), use `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders — never `?`. See CLAUDE.md gotcha #2.
- **Upsert pattern**: Single `INSERT INTO model_capabilities (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (provider, model_id) DO UPDATE SET ...` — no SELECT-then-INSERT. Two separate upsert statements needed (one for success=true, one for success=false) since they touch different columns (`last_succeeded_at` only on success).
- **Fire-and-forget error handling**: Function must never throw. Wrap in try/catch, log with `console.error('[model-registry] recordRunOutcome failed:', { provider, modelId, error: err.message })`. This matches the `[model-registry]` prefix pattern for log grep-ability.
- **Provider CHECK constraint**: The `model_capabilities` table has a CHECK constraint limiting provider to 6 allowed values (`anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `openrouter`, `ollama`, `github`). A constraint violation from an unexpected provider (e.g. Codex's implicit provider) should be logged distinctly so the caller knows provider derivation is wrong, not a DB outage.
- **Concurrency safety**: Multiple stories complete in parallel (wave execution), so the upsert's atomic `recent_success_count = model_capabilities.recent_success_count + 1` pattern avoids lost updates without needing explicit locking.
- **Caller site**: `execution-engine.ts` will call this after story pass/fail — it's already the sole execution engine for all agent types (claude/opencode/codex). The call should be fire-and-forget (`recordRunOutcome(...).catch(() => {})` or just `await` inside existing try/catch).
- **Return type**: Explicitly annotate `Promise<void>` — TypeScript strict mode is enabled, no implicit return types.

userStories.title: Implement recordProbeResult stub and module exports
userStories.description:
Add the recordProbeResult() Phase 2 stub to model-registry.ts and ensure all public types and functions are properly exported. The stub accepts probe data and writes it to the DB but is not called by any cron job yet — Phase 2 will add the actual probe scheduler.

**Convention guidance**: Named exports only — no default export from a non-component module. Group exports logically: types first, then functions. The stub should be a complete implementation (writes to DB) even though nothing calls it yet — this avoids a 'TODO' stub that bitrots. Follow the same try/catch + structured logging pattern as recordRunOutcome for consistency.

## Context
- **DB helper pattern**: Use `await execute(sql, params)` for the upsert — returns `{ rowCount }`. Use `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders (not `?`). The table is `model_capabilities` from MR-001's migration.
- **Upsert via `ON CONFLICT`**: PostgreSQL `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (provider, model_id) DO UPDATE SET ...` handles both the "update existing" and "insert if missing" acceptance criteria in a single statement — no need for a separate existence check.
- **Error handling pattern**: Mirror `recordRunOutcome` exactly — wrap the entire body in `try/catch`, log with `console.error('[model-registry] recordProbeResult failed:', err)` including context (provider, modelId), and swallow the error (never throws per AC).
- **Export ordering convention**: Group exports at the bottom of the file: types first (`ResolvedModel`, `RegisteredModel`, `ModelProvider`, `ModelCapabilitiesRow`), then functions (`resolveModel`, `listAvailableModels`, `recordRunOutcome`, `recordProbeResult`, `computeHealth`, `seedModelRegistry`). Named exports only — no `export default`.
- **Optional params**: Use `error?: string, latencyMs?: number` — not `error: string | undefined`. In the SQL, coalesce with `?? null` before passing as query params (`error ?? null`, `latencyMs ?? null`).
- **Default metric values on upsert-insert**: When the row doesn't exist, the `INSERT` side must set `recent_success_count = 0`, `recent_failure_count = 0` explicitly — don't rely on column defaults since the migration may not have them.
- **`seedModelRegistry` is a placeholder**: Export a stub function `async function seedModelRegistry(): Promise<void> {}` with a single-line comment `// MR-007: will seed initial model data` — keep it minimal, no TODO that bitrots.

userStories.title: Seed registry from Codex models_cache.json
userStories.description:
Implement the first seeder in seedModelRegistry() that reads ~/.codex/models_cache.json and upserts visible Codex models into model_capabilities. Only models with visibility='list' are seeded. The upsert is safe: it updates static fields (display_name, context_window_tokens) but never overwrites metric fields (recent_success_count, last_succeeded_at) to preserve historical accuracy.

**Convention guidance**: Use `os.homedir()` + `path.join()` for cross-platform path construction — never hardcode `/Users/...` or `~`. Use `fs.readFileSync` wrapped in try/catch for the JSON parse (not `import()` — it's a data file, not a module). Define an interface for the cache file shape (`CodexModelsCacheEntry`) rather than using `any`. Validate the parsed JSON shape before iterating — don't trust external file content. Use `console.warn` (not `console.log`) for missing-file warnings since it's a degraded-but-acceptable state.

## Context
- **Target file**: `backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts` — this is where `seedModelRegistry()` must be exported. Check if the file already exists and has a `model_capabilities` table interaction pattern to follow.
- **DB table**: `model_capabilities` with composite unique on `(provider, model_id)`. Use the existing `execute()` / `query()` helpers from `backend/src/db/index.ts` with `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders (not `?`). Always `await` DB calls.
- **Codex cache file reference**: Session 2026-04-07 documented GPT model selection reading from `~/.codex/models_cache.json`. The file is a JSON array of objects with `id`, `label`, `contextWindow`, `visibility` fields. Use `os.homedir()` + `path.join()` — never hardcode paths or use `~` tilde.

- **GREATEST() idempotency**: The `ON CONFLICT` upsert must use `GREATEST(existing, excluded)` for `recent_success_count`, `recent_failure_count`, and `last_succeeded_at`. This is the core invariant — restarting the backend or re-running `seedModelRegistry()` must never reduce counts.

userStories.title: Handle concurrent seed and query race condition at startup
userStories.description:
Address the race condition where HTTP requests arrive before seedModelRegistry() completes. During the seed window (potentially 1-3 seconds on a DB with 800+ pipeline_runs), resolveModel() queries an empty table and returns null for every model. This causes false negatives: valid models appear unavailable, enrichment silently substitutes, and pipeline triggers return 422 — all during the first few seconds after backend restart.

**Convention guidance**: Use a module-level Promise that resolveModel and listAvailableModels can optionally await. The flag should be an exported promise (not a boolean) so callers can await it without polling. Keep the solution simple — a boolean flag + retry is acceptable for Phase 1.

## Context
- **Race condition pattern**: Use a module-level `let seedPromise: Promise<void> | null = null` that `seedModelRegistry()` assigns on first call. `resolveModel()` and `listAvailableModels()` should `await Promise.race([seedPromise, timeout])` only when `seedPromise` is non-null and not yet settled. After settlement, subsequent calls skip the await entirely — check via a simple boolean flag (`let seedDone = false`) set in `.finally()`.

- **Timeout constant**: Define `const SEED_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000` at module top. Use `setTimeout` inside a `Promise.race` — do NOT use `AbortSignal.timeout()` (not available in all Node 20 builds). After timeout, log a warning (`logger.warn`) but proceed normally — partial data is better than a hung request.

- **Test environment safety**: If `seedModelRegistry()` is never called, `seedPromise` stays `null` and both `resolveModel()`/`listAvailableModels()` skip the await entirely, falling through to direct DB queries. Do NOT initialize `seedPromise` to a pre-resolved promise — that masks the "seed never called" case in tests.

- **Existing seed call site**: `seedModelRegistry()` is called during server startup in `server.ts`. It runs `enrichAllModels()` which scans `pipeline_runs` + `token_usage` for historically-used models — this is the slow path (~1-3s on 800+ runs). The promise must capture this entire operation, not just the DB query portion.

- **No polling / no intervals**: The convention guidance explicitly says "exported promise, not a boolean" for the public API. Internally use a boolean for the fast-path check (`if (seedDone) return` before `await`), but export the promise so integration tests can `await seedComplete` deterministically.

- **Error handling**: If `seedModelRegistry()` throws, the promise should still resolve (not reject) — set `seedDone = true` in `.finally()`. A failed seed means the registry falls back to static `SUPPORTED_MODELS` data, which is acceptable. Rejecting would cause every `resolveModel()` caller to throw, cascading 500s across all pipeline triggers.

- **RLS context**: This module runs on the backend pool (`db/index.ts` pool), not through `withUserClient()`. No RLS concerns here — model registry is a system-level table, not workspace-scoped. Keep using `query<T>()` / `queryOne<T>()` helpers directly.

- **Concurrency edge case**: Multiple concurrent requests arriving during the seed window should all await the *same* promise instance — do NOT create a new promise per caller. The module-level singleton pattern handles this naturally.
acceptanceCriteria: model-registry.ts exports a seedComplete promise that resolves when seedModelRegistry() finishes (successfully or with error)
resolveModel() checks if seedComplete has resolved; if not, awaits it with a 5-second timeout before querying the DB
listAvailableModels() has the same seedComplete await behavior as resolveModel()
If the seed takes longer than 5 seconds, resolveModel and listAvailableModels proceed with whatever data is available (partial seed is better than blocking forever)
The 5-second timeout is a named constant (SEED_TIMEOUT_MS) not a magic number
After the seed completes, all subsequent resolveModel calls skip the await (no per-request overhead)
If seedModelRegistry is never called (e.g. in test environments), resolveModel still works — it just queries the DB directly without waiting

userStories.title: Validate provider value in recordRunOutcome against CHECK constraint
userStories.description:
The model_capabilities table has a CHECK constraint limiting provider to 6 specific values. recordRunOutcome upserts rows, meaning it can INSERT new rows. If the derived provider (from deriveProvider in execution-engine.ts) produces a value outside the CHECK constraint (e.g. a new agent type like 'gemini' or a typo), the INSERT will throw a Postgres constraint violation error. While recordRunOutcome has a try/catch, the error is logged but the root cause (wrong provider derivation) is obscured. Add explicit validation of the provider value before the DB call.

**Convention guidance**: Use the ModelProvider type union as the validation source — check that the runtime value matches one of the union members. This is a runtime check since the value comes from string parsing (deriveProvider), not from type-safe code.

## Context
- **Target file**: `backend/src/lib/model-capability-registry.ts` — contains both `recordRunOutcome` and `recordProbeResult` functions that upsert into `model_capabilities` table
- **ModelProvider type location**: Check `backend/src/lib/model-capability-registry.ts` for the `ModelProvider` type union definition. Extract the literal values into a `const MODEL_PROVIDERS = ['codex', 'claude', 'opencode', 'anthropic', 'openai', 'openrouter'] as const` array, then derive the type from it (`type ModelProvider = typeof MODEL_PROVIDERS[number]`). This ensures the validation set and type stay in sync — adding a new provider to the array automatically updates both.
- **deriveProvider source**: `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts` has `deriveProvider()` which parses the model string at runtime — its output is untyped (`string`), so runtime validation is essential before DB insertion
- **CHECK constraint**: The `model_capabilities` table has `CHECK (provider IN ('codex','claude','opencode','anthropic','openai','openrouter'))` — a constraint violation throws a Postgres error that gets caught by the existing try/catch but obscures the root cause
- **Pattern**: Use `const VALID_PROVIDERS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(MODEL_PROVIDERS)` and guard with `if (!VALID_PROVIDERS.has(provider))` before the upsert. Log with `console.warn('[model-registry] Invalid provider …', { provider, modelId })` and `return` early — do NOT throw, since these functions are called in non-critical post-run telemetry paths
- **Apply to both functions**: `recordRunOutcome` and `recordProbeResult` both accept a provider param and both hit the same table — add the identical guard to both, or extract a shared `validateProvider()` helper if the check is more than 2 lines
- **No shortcuts**: Per project convention (`feedback_no_shortcuts.md`), fix the root cause (validate before DB call) rather than just improving the catch block's error message
acceptanceCriteria: recordRunOutcome validates that provider is one of the 6 allowed values ('codex','claude','opencode','anthropic','openai','openrouter') before executing the SQL upsert
If provider is not in the allowed set, logs console.warn('[model-registry] Invalid provider in recordRunOutcome:', { provider, modelId }) and returns without hitting the DB
The allowed provider set is derived from the ModelProvider type definition — not a separate hardcoded array — so adding a new provider to the type automatically adds it to the validation
recordProbeResult has the same provider validation as recordRunOutcome
The validation uses a Set or array includes check — not a chain of === comparisons

userStories.title: Preserve codex-models endpoint hardcoded fallback
userStories.description:
The current GET /api/config/codex-models endpoint (config.ts lines 1351-1356) has a hardcoded fallback array of 4 Codex models returned when ~/.codex/models_cache.json doesn't exist. MR-007 skips the codex seed when the file is missing. MR-011 switches the endpoint to use listAvailableModels(). Combined, these three changes mean: no cache file → no codex seed → listAvailableModels returns empty → empty dropdown. This is a regression from today's behavior where the dropdown always shows at least 4 models. This story ensures the hardcoded fallback models are always seeded into the registry, regardless of whether the cache file exists.

**Convention guidance**: The simplest fix is in seedModelRegistry — always upsert the 4 known Codex models as a baseline, then overlay with cache file data if available. The fallback models should be a const array in model-registry.ts, not imported from config.ts.

## Context
- **Model Registry location**: The `model-registry.ts` file is the canonical home for model capability data and seed logic — define `CODEX_FALLBACK_MODELS` as a top-level `const` array there, not in `config.ts`. The 4 known models are `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `o3` (verify exact IDs by reading the existing hardcoded array in `config.ts` lines 1351-1356 before implementing).
- **Seed ordering matters**: In `seedModelRegistry()`, upsert the 4 fallback models *first*, then overlay with `~/.codex/models_cache.json` data if the file exists. Use `ON CONFLICT (model_id, provider) DO UPDATE` so cache metadata (display_name, context_window_tokens) wins when present.
- **Spec model resolution chain**: Per `spec_model_resolution.md`, canonical resolution is `story.model → spec.model → RORCA_MODEL env`. The codex-models endpoint is UI-only (populates dropdowns) — it does NOT affect execution-time model selection. Don't conflate the two.
- **Codex CLI gotcha**: Per memory from 2026-04-07, Codex invocation is `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -m <model>`. `RORCA_MODEL` is ignored for codex agent type — the subscription model is used. The dropdown still matters for UX clarity (showing what's available).
- **Don't break the existing config.ts endpoint**: `GET /api/config/codex-models` currently works by reading `models_cache.json` with a hardcoded fallback. After this change, it should call `listAvailableModels({ provider: 'codex' })` from the registry — but the 4 models must always be present. Verify the endpoint returns at least 4 models in both scenarios (cache exists / cache missing).
- **Migration not needed**: Model capabilities are seeded at runtime via `seedModelRegistry()` (called on backend startup), not via SQL migrations. No new migration file required.
- **Edge case — empty registry on first boot**: If the backend starts before `seedModelRegistry()` completes and a request hits `/api/config/codex-models`, the response could be empty. Ensure the seed runs synchronously during startup (before Express begins accepting requests), or handle the race gracefully.

The fallback models are defined as a const array (CODEX_FALLBACK_MODELS) in model-registry.ts — not imported from config.ts

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
# Model Capability Registry — Phase 1

## Problem
Today, model availability is implicit: each provider's local cache (e.g. `~/.codex/models_cache.json`) is read directly by the API and trusted as truth. The picker shows whatever the cache advertises. Validation happens at execution time — too late. When a spec is created with a stale or mistyped model ID (e.g. `gpt-5.4` typed externally, or a Codex model that the local CLI binary can't actually invoke), all downstream code paths fail in their own scattered way:
- Enrichment swallows 14 LLM errors silently in `Promise.allSettled` and returns `storiesEnriched: 0` with no surfaced reason.
- Pipeline triggers spawn agents that die with cryptic CLI errors hours after queueing.
- The UI dropdown lies: it offers models that the running binary cannot execute.

The user just hit this on `classification-autoresearch-v2-eval-hardening` — spec was created with `model: "gpt-5.4"`, all 14 enrichment calls failed, no error reached the UI.

A complicating reality: actual production runs with `codex/gpt-5.4` succeed (30 runs, 535 stories, recent runs 100% pass). A naive "ping probe" would falsely mark the model unavailable and hide it from the picker — breaking working workflows.

## Goal
Build a **Model Capability Registry**: one DB table that is the single source of truth for "what models can this Rorca install actually use." Every code path that touches a model ID — UI dropdown, spec generate, spec enrich, pipeline trigger, execution-engine spawn — resolves through this registry. Probe data is one input, but historical run success rate is weighted higher.

## Phase 1 scope (this spec, ~6 stories)
This is the **indirection + retrofit** phase. Probe service is stubbed (always returns "healthy"). Real probes ship in Phase 2.

### Story 1 — Migration: `model_capabilities` table
Create `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/<timestamp>_create_model_capabilities.sql`.
Columns: `provider TEXT NOT NULL` (codex|claude|opencode|anthropic|openai|openrouter), `model_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `display_name TEXT`, `context_window_tokens INTEGER`, `requires_subscription BOOL`, `requires_api_key BOOL`, `tier TEXT`, `last_probed_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `probe_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'` (healthy|degraded|unavailable|unknown), `probe_error TEXT`, `probe_latency_ms INTEGER`, `recent_success_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `recent_failure_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `last_succeeded_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()`, `updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()`.
Primary key: `(provider, model_id)`. Index on `probe_status`.

### Story 2 — `model-registry.ts` library
Create `backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts` with:
- `resolveModel(requestedId, opts?) → Promise<ResolvedModel | null>`: returns the model if registered and not `unavailable`; returns null if unknown or unavailable. `opts.allowDegraded` defaults true.
- `listAvailableModels(opts) → Promise<RegisteredModel[]>`: filtered by `provider`, `probe_status`, etc.
- `recordRunOutcome(provider, modelId, success: boolean)`: increments `recent_success_count` or `recent_failure_count`, updates `last_succeeded_at` on success. Called from execution-engine after each story.
- `recordProbeResult(provider, modelId, status, error?, latencyMs?)`: stub for Phase 2 probe service.
- `computeHealth(row) → 'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable'`: composite scoring — never marks unavailable if `recent_success_count` in last 7 days > 5, regardless of probe_status.

### Story 3 — Seed registry from existing sources
On backend startup, run `seedModelRegistry()`:
- Read `~/.codex/models_cache.json`, upsert visible models with `provider='codex'`, `requires_subscription=true`, `probe_status='unknown'`.
- Read `ALL_MODELS` from `llm-client.ts`, upsert with appropriate provider per model.
- Backfill: scan distinct `(agent_type, agent_model)` from `pipeline_runs` over the last 30 days; upsert any combos found, set `last_succeeded_at` from most recent successful run, set `recent_success_count` from `story_results` joined on those runs where `status='pass'`.
- This means the gpt-5.4 entry will already show 535 successful stories on first registry load — protecting it from being hidden.

### Story 4 — Retrofit `/api/config/codex-models` and friends
Replace the `models_cache.json`-direct read in `backend/src/routes/config.ts:1335` with a `listAvailableModels({ provider: 'codex' })` call. The cache becomes a *seeder*, not the API response. Same treatment for any other endpoint that returns model lists to the UI. Filter to `probe_status IN ('healthy', 'degraded', 'unknown')` by default; expose a `?includeUnavailable=true` flag.

### Story 5 — Retrofit `/api/specs/:specId/enrich` and spec generate
In `backend/src/routes/specs.ts`, replace `isValidModel()` with `resolveModel()`. If the spec's `model` is unknown or unavailable, log a warning and fall back to `DEFAULT_MODEL` (existing behavior, but now backed by the registry instead of a static `SUPPORTED_MODELS` array). Same retrofit for `POST /api/specs/generate` model validation. Surface the substitution in the response payload (`{ requestedModel, actualModel, substitutionReason }`) so the UI can show a banner.

### Story 6 — Retrofit pipeline trigger + execution-engine + outcome recording
- `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` calls `resolveModel()` before queueing. If unavailable, return `422` with `{ error, code: 'MODEL_UNAVAILABLE', requestedModel, suggestedFallback }`. Do not silently substitute at trigger time — the user needs to know.
- `execution-engine.ts` calls `recordRunOutcome(provider, modelId, true|false)` at the end of each story (success path: in story-pass branch; failure path: in story-failed/skipped branch). This is what keeps `gpt-5.4`-style "probes lie but reality works" models from being hidden.
- Add structured logging: every `resolveModel()` decision logs `{ requestedModel, resolvedModel, probeStatus, recentSuccesses }` for auditability.

## Out of scope (Phase 2)
- Real probe service (1-token ping per provider, cron-driven).
- UI status dots in model picker.
- Vault-key validity probing.
- MCP server tool-availability probing.
- Per-workspace model overrides.

## Acceptance
- Backend type-check passes.
- After backend restart on a fresh cashflow workspace: `model_capabilities` table contains `(codex, gpt-5.4)` with `recent_success_count >= 30`, `last_succeeded_at` from the most recent codex/gpt-5.4 run.
- `GET /api/config/codex-models` returns the same 4 models it returns today, sourced from the registry not the cache file.
- Creating a spec with `model: "gpt-9.9-fake"` and calling enrich returns `200` with annotations using `DEFAULT_MODEL` and a warning in the response body explaining the substitution. (Today: silent failure.)
- `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` with a fake model returns 422 with `code: MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (Today: queues the run and dies hours later in the worker.)
- All existing cashflow runs still execute with their original `(agent_type, agent_model)` — no regressions.

## Files most likely to change
- `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/<timestamp>_create_model_capabilities.sql` (new)
- `backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/routes/config.ts` (retrofit codex-models endpoint)
- `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` (retrofit enrich + generate; remove `isValidModel` fallback added today)
- `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts` (outcome recording at story-end branches)
- `backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts` (422 on MODEL_UNAVAILABLE at trigger time)
- `backend/src/server.ts` or equivalent startup: call `seedModelRegistry()` once

## Constraints / non-obvious gotchas
- `pipeline_runs.agent_model` is a TEXT column with no FK to the registry. Don't add a FK in this spec — too much migration risk on 800+ existing rows. Registry is read-side only.
- Codex `models_cache.json` lists models as `visibility: list | hide`. Only seed `list` ones, but allow `hide` ones to be added later via `recordRunOutcome` if a hidden model somehow runs successfully.
- The seed function must be idempotent — backend restarts shouldn't reset `recent_success_count` or `last_succeeded_at`. Use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (provider, model_id) DO UPDATE` only for static fields (display_name, context_window), not the metric fields.
- `claude --print --model <id>` rejects non-Claude IDs at exec time. Phase 2 probes will catch this; for Phase 1, the `provider` column carries the routing intent.
